sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Philosophical Stance**: Dadu Dayal was a **Nirguna Bhakti** saint, advocating for a formless God (Parabrahma) and rejecting idol worship, caste hierarchies, and priestly dominance.
• **Literary Contribution**: His teachings are compiled in the **Dadu Anubhav Vani** and **Dadu Dayal ki Bani**, primarily written in **Dhundhari** (a dialect of Rajasthani) with influences of Braj and Hindi.
• **Institutional Framework**: He established the **Dadu Panth**, which organized followers into a disciplined order, later categorized into sub-sects like Khalsa, Nagas, and Viraktas.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement acted as a socio-cultural bridge in Rajasthan, promoting communal harmony between Hindus and Muslims during the Mughal era.

items.definition: The primary center of the Dadu Panth in Rajasthan, serving as the spiritual headquarters where Dadu Dayal spent his final years.
The followers of Dadu Dayal who emphasize 'Satnam' (True Name) and maintain a simple, egalitarian lifestyle.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Social Reform**: Active dismantling of the caste system by accepting disciples from all backgrounds, including Muslims.
• **Literary Synthesis**: Use of vernacular languages to make spiritual knowledge accessible to the common masses (Lok-bhasha).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Historical marginalization of Nirguna traditions compared to Saguna Vaishnavism.
• **Solutions**: Academic preservation of Dadu-vani manuscripts and digital archiving of regional Bhakti literature.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content: • **Memory Acronym**: 'D-A-D-U' -> **D**hundhari language, **A**dvocate of Nirguna, **D**isciples from all castes, **U**nified Rajasthan.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Dadu Dayal with Saguna saints. Remember: Dadu Dayal was a Nirguna saint, similar to Kabir, not a Saguna Vaishnava saint like Tulsidas or Surdas.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Socio-Religious Egalitarianism' when discussing Dadu Dayal's contribution to medieval Indian social structure.

keyTakeaways: Dadu Dayal was a 16th-century Nirguna saint from Rajasthan.
His teachings emphasized monotheism and social equality, rejecting caste and idol worship.
The Dadu Panth is his institutional legacy, characterized by sub-sects like the Nagas.
